clue.text: Entitlement to enter good French or English city

indicators.note: the entitlement word is told to go into the French word, so it sits inside it

parts.note: bon is the French for good
a right is something you are entitled to

explanation.surface: Someone debating whether a claim to a fine French or English city holds good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is only a link word here, joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Brighton is a seaside city on the south coast of England.

clue.text: Parrot to have hidden under material

indicators.note: in a down clue, the piece said to be under another is written below it, so it comes second

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric used for upholstery and ties
to have food hidden away, or put away, is to eat it

explanation.surface: An instruction to make a parrot keep something concealed beneath some cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: Food that is 'put away' has been eaten, the idea behind 'have hidden'.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to say again what one has heard, exactly as a repeat does.

clue.text: Cunning guy will, from what we hear

indicators.note: signals that the clue words are to be spoken and the spelling taken from their sound

parts.note: said quickly, guy will runs together as guy'll

explanation.surface: A sly fellow's last testament, as rumour has it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy'll', the contraction of 'guy will', is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name crafty, deceitful cleverness, so they are synonyms as nouns.

clue.text: See artist struggling with compositions

indicators.note: the words see and artist are in difficulty, so their letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Watch a painter battling with how to arrange a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compositions' looks like art or music, but here it means written essays.
explanation.definitionFit: A composition can be a written piece, and formal written studies of a subject are treatises.

clue.text: I may be seen as the first one that's positive

definitions.text: I may be seen as the first one that's positive

parts.words: I may be seen as the first one that's positive
parts.note: the letter I is the Roman way to write one, the first positive whole number

explanation.surface: An optimist claiming to be the first upbeat person around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' looks like the speaker but is the Roman figure for 1.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure or symbol standing for a number, such as the Roman I, is a numeral.

clue.text: A theologian I brought to court as sort of abuser?

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theology degree

explanation.surface: A churchman and I took someone to court on an abuse charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that abuser is a loose fit: the substance abuser.
explanation.definitionFit: A person dependent on drugs or drink is a substance abuser, hence the hinted kind of abuser.

clue.text: Try when given influence in decision-making

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
having a say means some influence over a decision

explanation.surface: Advice to have a go once you get some voice in the decisions.
explanation.definitionFit: To assay is to attempt or test something, so it is a synonym of try.

clue.text: Speech-maker got back, having switched ends

indicators.note: the first and last letters of the word for got back change places

parts.note: to have got something back is to have reclaimed it

explanation.surface: An orator recovered, having changed sides at both ends.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first and last letters move: R and D swap places.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who declaims delivers a formal oration, so is a speech-maker.

clue.text: Cold and inexperienced, Heather is moving slowly

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a raw recruit is an inexperienced one
ling is another name for common heather

explanation.surface: A chilly novice called Heather is making her way at a snail's pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name but is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: To crawl is to move very slowly, as on hands and knees or in traffic.

clue.text: Troublemaker showing ill-feeling around back of bar

indicators.note: the spite word goes around the letter taken from bar

parts.note: spite is malicious ill-feeling

indicators.note: points to the final letter of bar

explanation.surface: A rowdy drinker displaying resentment near the rear of the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprite is a mischievous elf or fairy, a supernatural troublemaker.

clue.text: Person of note going from bar to bar

definitions.text: Person of note going from bar to bar

parts.words: Person of note going from bar to bar
parts.note: a player of music notes moves from one measure, or bar, of the score to the next

explanation.surface: A well-known figure on a pub crawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Person of note' suggests someone famous and 'bar' a pub; both are musical terms here.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer reads notes and plays through the bars of a piece of music.

clue.text: Mum, more elegant, seen as dangerous woman

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
neater means tidier or more elegant

explanation.surface: A smartly turned-out mother is regarded as a menace.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-eater is a woman who seduces and discards men, so dangerous to them.

clue.text: Yen to get ahead of schedule producing annual publication

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese currency the yen
early means before the expected time

explanation.surface: A longing to get in front of the timetable results in a yearbook.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, a yearly is a periodical issued once a year.

clue.text: Enlisted with camp reorganised in movement to a different location

indicators.note: the letters of enlisted and camp are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Recruits with their base rearranged during a relocation.
explanation.definitionFit: Displacement is the shifting of something or someone out of their usual place.

clue.text: Set of rules for some who are buttoned up?

definitions.text: Set of rules for some who are buttoned up?

parts.words: Set of rules for some who are buttoned up?
parts.note: buttoned up suggests reserved people, but literally means wearing fastened clothes, as required by rules of attire

explanation.surface: A rulebook for the strait-laced and reserved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buttoned up' reads as prim, but means wearing done-up clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Rules on what clothes must be worn at a venue or event form this set.

clue.text: Trick proposal made by candidate

parts.note: a con is a swindle or trick
a tender is a formal offer or proposal to do work

explanation.surface: A deceitful offer put forward by someone standing for election.
explanation.definitionFit: A contender is someone competing for a post or title, as a candidate is.

clue.text: Very little energy in second part of symphony

indicators.note: the very and energy letters go inside the word for second

parts.note: a second, or a moment, is a brief time
E, a small form of energy, is its symbol in physics

explanation.surface: The symphony's second section has hardly any energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' looks like it qualifies 'part' but gives MOMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A symphony is divided into self-contained sections called movements.

clue.text: One sort of spider that brings in the cash

definitions.meaning: a small spider, said to bring luck with money, has this alternative name
a business or product that earns plenty of money

explanation.surface: A spider that makes you rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the tiny lucky spider and a profitable venture carry this name.

clue.text: With mischief-makers around, death is about to happen

indicators.note: the mischief-makers word goes around the death word

parts.note: imps are mischievous little devils
end can mean death, as in 'came to a sad end'

explanation.surface: With little devils about, the grim reaper is near.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that impends is imminent, threatening to occur soon.

clue.text: Love in wood is pleasurable experience

indicators.note: the love letter goes inside the word for a wood

parts.note: a grove is a small wood
love is nil in tennis, so the letter O

explanation.surface: Romance among the trees is a delight.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang, a groove is something very enjoyable, as in 'it was a groove'.

clue.text: Let out, learner relaxed

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate
eased means slackened or relaxed

explanation.surface: A trainee driver let off the leash and calmer.
explanation.definitionFit: Property that is let out to a tenant on a contract has been rented out.

clue.text: Doctor with one foot under pile of snow?

indicators.note: in a down clue, the pieces said to be under the doctor come after it

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A physician with a foot buried in a snowdrift.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a pile of snow is one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Wind heaps snow into banks called snowdrifts, so this is one kind of pile.

clue.text: Hip teacher — he put out zany diagram for maths class

indicators.note: the letters of he are to be removed from the fodder
crazy, so the remaining letters of hip teacher are muddled up

explanation.surface: A trendy teacher, lacking a man, produces a wacky chart for a lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: Take H and E out of HIPTEACHER and shuffle the remaining letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A circle divided into slices showing proportions is a classic graph taught in mathematics.

clue.text: Servant trashing hotel

indicators.note: wrecking the word hotel throws its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A staff member wrecking the hotel he works at.
explanation.definitionFit: A helot was a serf in ancient Sparta, so a servant or slave.

clue.text: Scripture this person smuggled into county, showing commitment

indicators.note: the scripture and person letters are sneaked inside the county

parts.note: Devon is a county in south-west England
OT is the Old Testament, part of scripture
the setter refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: Someone sneaking a Bible into a shire, a sign of their faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Devotion is loyal, wholehearted dedication, which is commitment.

clue.text: University lecturer is key-holder, a renowned chemist

indicators.note: the lecturer is the holder of the key, so the lecturer word contains the key word

parts.note: a don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge
Alt is a key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: An academic holds the keys, and he is also a famous scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key-holder' means DON holds ALT; John Dalton devised atomic theory.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dalton was an English chemist famous for his atomic theory.

clue.text: Way something wooden is implanted into stone

indicators.note: the wooden thing goes inside the stone letters

parts.note: st is the abbreviation of stone, the British weight of 14 pounds
a tree is made of wood

explanation.surface: A method of setting a timber object into rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Way is a common name for a road, as in Appian Way, and a street is a road.

clue.text: Proud walker — good person accompanying king, say

parts.note: St is a saint, a good person
R is short for rex, Latin for king
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: A saint walking with a monarch, holding his head up.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who struts walks in a stiff, swaggering, self-important way.
